summary: Frontend-only test of the new Map Settings feature (Settings > Maps tab) on the preview URL as admin@example.com. Verified: provider dropdown, conditional Google API key field, empty-key validation, save + persistence across reload, and live tile-source switching on all three maps (Post Site LocationMapPicker, Live Tracking, public officer /shift mini map) for both Google and OSM. All checks passed; setting left on OpenStreetMap.
critical_code_review_comments: MapSettingsTab: initial GET /settings failure is silently swallowed (.catch(() => {})) — the tab then shows default 'osm' even when the saved provider is Google, which can mislead an admin into overwriting real settings. Add an error toast / retry state.

Google Maps API key is returned in plain text by GET /settings and rendered in a type='text' input; consider masking (or returning a masked value) since the key is billable and visible to anyone with settings access.
Saving with provider='osm' keeps the previously saved Google key in the DB (field is only hidden). Acceptable, but not obvious to the user — a hint that the key is retained would help.
seed_data_creation: None. No records created (Add Post Site dialog opened only to inspect the map; not submitted).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified results: (1) Settings > Maps card [map-settings-tab] renders; provider select [map-provider-select]; key field [google-key-field]/[google-maps-api-key-input] only rendered when provider=google (count 0 for OSM). (2) Google selected with empty key -> error toast 'Enter a Google Maps API key to use Google Maps.' and NO save. (3) Google + key -> 'Map settings saved'; after full reload provider and key persisted. (4) With provider=google+key, tiles from all 3 maps came from mt{0-3}.google.com/vt: PostSite, Live Tracking and /shift/maptest224fb457 mini map. (5) After switching to OpenStreetMap + Save, all 3 maps served {a,b,c}.tile.openstreetmap.org tiles and the settings tab reloaded as OpenStreetMap with the key field hidden. NOTE: at the start of this run the persisted provider was already 'google' with key AIzaSyDRbp9-4U3i5XjBqu-cTg5JBXJBfO4nEks (contrary to the request note saying it was OSM) — so the 'default OSM' fresh-install case was not observable in UI; it was left as google-key-in-db + provider=osm at the end. Use wait_until='domcontentloaded' + wait_for_selector for the /shift page (1s ticker prevents networkidle).
